description: TAP-11 §3 manifest validation, including the text rules (§3.5) and the parameter schema (§3.6). Each case gives the manifest as JSON text and the expected result: valid, or manifest-invalid with its reason (§2.3). knownText is what §3.4 lets a client present (members this TAP does not define are left out). calls give arguments checked against inputs before sending (§3.6): null means the client may send, otherwise the reason it refuses; paramsText, when present, is the JSON text of the arguments and is judged with its number lexemes. A case with `generate` has its manifest text built as prefix + unit repeated count times + suffix. `quotes` give provider text and the string literal §3.4 item 2 makes of it; `urls` give strings checked against §3.5 item 5 alone (valid, or reason bad-url). Addresses and signatures are placeholders: binding (§2.2 step 5), delegation (§4) and content signature (§5) are not checked here. Non-ASCII code points are written as \u escapes. The note text is informative.

"a", U+0897, U+0323: U+0897 is unassigned in Unicode 15.1.0, so it has combining class 0, blocks the composition of U+0323 and the string is NFC under the pinned tables. Implementations of Unicode 16 or later give it class 230, reorder it after U+0323 and call the string not NFC; that disagreement is why §3.5 pins the version.
"a", U+0301 (class 230), U+0323 (class 220): NFC reorders and composes them.
Hangul syllable written as three conjoining jamo; NFC is U+D55C.

"x" with U+0301: no precomposed form exists, so the string is NFC.
U+E0FFF is unassigned but Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (the whole range U+E0000 to U+E0FFF is).

cases.note: uint53 is judged on the JSON text of the argument: `0` or a nonzero digit followed by digits, with a value of at most 2^53 - 1. `1.0` and `1e0` have the value 1 but are refused, as is `-0`.
Nesting depth 32 (the manifest object counts as 1) is the limit.
Depth 33 is `limit-exceeded`.
30,000 nested arrays in an unknown member (about 60 KB, under the size limit): a named result, not a crash. The manifest text is the prefix, the unit repeated `count` times, then the suffix.
U+000A is allowed only in the `description` of a method descriptor, not in a member of that name elsewhere.
